```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(beFAIR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# All chunks run from inside the FAIRground directory
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "beFAIR_project")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = dir)
```

A **FAIRground** is the combination of three things: a structured directory on
disk, a SQL database, and a set of R ETL scripts that move data from raw files
into the database. This guide shows how to create each of them from scratch.

---

## 1. Create the project directory

```{r start-project, message=FALSE}
startProject(dir = dir)
list.files(dir)
```

`startProject()` creates the standard FAIRground layout:

| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `studies/` | Clinical trial metadata — participants, arms, design |
| `experiments/` | Laboratory measurements (CyTOF, ELISA, Olink, …) |
| `analyses/` | Derived results computed from study and experiment data |
| `common/` | Shared reference files |
| `codebooks/` | Custom YAML codebooks for project-specific tables |
| `logs/` | JSON run logs written by `databaseUpdate()` |

---

## 2. Connect and initialise the database

```{r connect-init}
con <- FAIRgroundConnect(drv = RSQLite::SQLite(), dsn = ":memory:")
databaseInitialize()
DBI::dbListTables(con)
```

`databaseInitialize()` creates the registry tables that beFAIR uses to track
codebook versions (`table_codebook`) and ETL scripts (`table_script`). You only
run this once when setting up a new database.

> **In production** you would connect via a DSN:
> `FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")`. On Windows, configure DSNs in the ODBC
> Data Sources administrator.

---

## 3. Register a study

```{r add-study, message=FALSE}
addStudy(study_name = "MyStudy", study_id = "MYST1")
list.files("studies/MyStudy")
```

`addStudy()` creates a folder under `studies/` and drafts the four mandatory
ETL scripts:

```{r list-scripts}
list.files("studies/MyStudy/scripts")
```

| Script | What it populates |
|---|---|
| `id_mapping.R` | Maps raw source IDs to pseudonymous `participant_id` values |
| `participant.R` | One row per participant — demographics, enrolment, BMI |
| `studyarm.R` | The study arms (control, treatment groups, dosing cohorts) |
| `studydesign.R` | Scheduled timepoints and events in the trial protocol |

Each script is a template: the codebook structure and boilerplate are
pre-filled, and you complete the data-mapping logic for your specific raw files.
See [Adding a study](adding_a_study.html) for a full walkthrough of each script.

---

## 4. Fill in the study metadata

`addStudy()` also creates a `meta.yaml` file with fields you should complete:

```{r meta, echo=FALSE}
meta_path <- "studies/MyStudy/meta.yaml"
cat(paste(readLines(meta_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

If the study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, pass the registration code and
beFAIR will pre-fill the relevant metadata automatically:

```r
addStudy(study_name = "MyStudy", study_id = "MYST1",
         registration_code = "NCT02237586")
```

---

## 5. Run the update

Once your ETL scripts are complete, `databaseUpdate()` runs them all, validates
the output, and loads the results:

```r
databaseUpdate()
```

You re-run this command whenever scripts change or new data arrives. beFAIR
detects which scripts have changed (via MD5 hash), skips anything unchanged, and
only reloads what is new or updated.
